title: Incident records
description: Every incident of the services in services/*.yml, read by scripts/build_status.py. Text on this file is public once the status page is published: describe what happened to the system, never who caused it, and leave out internal host names, addresses and customer names.

when.description: UTC. A date alone when the time was not recorded; a time only when a record backs it (an alert, a log line, a deploy).

id.description: YYYY-MM-DD-short-name, the start date and two to five words

title.description: What users saw, in one line

services.description: Catalogue ids of the services users saw fail

impact.description: Impact on users. none changes no state on the status page

severity.description: Internal severity, set by the incident lead

resolved.description: Set exactly when the last update has stage resolved

summary.description: What happened to the system and what users saw, without blame

updates.description: Public updates in order. Stages only go forward: investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved. A stage can repeat.

postmortem.description: doc:<space>/<slug> or URL of the postmortem

incidents.title: Checkout failed for some users
incidents.summary: A configuration change cut the database connection pool from 50 to 5 connections. During the morning peak the API ran out of connections and about 18% of checkout requests failed with errors until the change was rolled back.

updates.text: Some checkouts fail with an error. We are looking into it.
A configuration change reduced the database connections of the API. We are rolling it back.
The rollback is out and the error rate is back to normal. We are watching it.
Checkout works for all users again.
